title: Sheaves of modules on the small etale site have enough injectives
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $T_{\Et}$ its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], $R$ a commutative ring, $R_T$ the constant sheaf of rings with value $R$ on $T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and $\Mod(T_{\Et},R)=\Mod(R_T)$ the abelian category of sheaves of $R_T$-modules on $T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then $\Mod(T_{\Et},R)$ has enough injectives: for every object $F$ there are an injective object $J$ of $\Mod(T_{\Et},R)$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions] and a monomorphism $F\hookrightarrow J$ in $\Mod(T_{\Et},R)$. In particular the category $\Ab(T_{\Et})$ of abelian sheaves on $T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] has enough injectives.

source.place: Injectives, Theorem 079H (label theorem-injective-embedding-grothendieck: a Grothendieck abelian category has functorial injective embeddings), applied to Mod(O) via Modules on Sites, Lemmas 03DA, 03DB, 03EW (literature/stacks-project/sites-modules.tex); the direct statement for any ringed site is Injectives, Theorem 01DU (label theorem-sheaves-modules-injectives); used in Etale Cohomology, Lemma 0A4C (label lemma-sandwich), proof, first paragraph

proof.text: *$\Mod(T_{\Et},R)$ and $\Ab(T_{\Et})$ are Grothendieck abelian.* By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-grothendieck-abelian] with $\Lambda=R$, the category $\Mod(T_{\Et},R)$ of sheaves of $R_T$-modules is a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]: it is abelian, has all small colimits, filtered colimits in it are exact, and it has a generator ($\bigoplus_U j_{U!}R_U$ over a set of representatives $U$ of an essentially small dense subcategory of $T_{\Et}$). The same lemma (its case $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$) says that $\Ab(T_{\Et})$ is Grothendieck abelian.

source.place: Modules on Sites, Lemmas 03DA, 03DB, 03EW (3), as collected in node lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-grothendieck-abelian; cf. Cohomology on Sites, proof of Lemma 07AC (sites-cohomology.tex): 'the category of modules on a ringed site is a Grothendieck abelian category'

proof.text: *Enough injectives.* A Grothendieck abelian category has enough injectives [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives] (Stacks 079H: it even has a functorial injective embedding, i.e. a functor $M\mapsto I(M)$ with $I(M)$ injective and a natural monomorphism $i_M:M\to I(M)$; taking $J=I(F)$ and $F\hookrightarrow J$ the map $i_F$ gives the statement for each $F$). Applied to the two Grothendieck abelian categories of step 1, $\Mod(T_{\Et},R)$ and $\Ab(T_{\Et})$ have enough injectives, with injectivity in the sense of [def-sp-injective-resolutions] taken inside the respective category.
